newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to discuss E.Timor with U.N. chief.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to discuss E.Timor with U.N. chief.

text.p: Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said on Tuesday he and United Nations chief Kofi Annan would discuss the future of U.N.-sponsored talks with Portugal on East Timor in Switzerland next week.
Alatas will attend the World Economic Forum meeting in Davos, Switzerland from January 30 to February 4.
He told reporters after meeting President Suharto that Annan was also due to be in Davos, and he expected to discuss the East Timor issue with the new U.N. secretary-general.
"I expect to meet the secretary-general at the Davos meeting... I will ask about future talks on East Timor with Portugal," Alatas said.
He accused Portugal of trying to drag out the East Timor issue and attempting to blame Indonesia for the lack of a settlement.
The two countries were due to hold the latest in a series of meetings on East Timor in New York in December, but the meeting was postponed and a date has still to be decided.

The U.N.-sponsored talks have continued for several years since Indonesia's invasion of the former Portuguese colony of East Timor in December 1975 and the territory's incorporation into Indonesia as its 27th province the following July.
The United Nations did not recognise the move and still regards Portugal as the territory's administering power.
Tensions in the East Timor capital of Dili have risen recently as Indonesian security officers continued their search for youths suspected of involvement in the murder of a soldier on December 24.
The official Antara news agency said the dossier of 16 men believed to have been involved had been handed by police to the district attorney there on Tuesday.
"We have submitted the dossier of the 16 main suspects. The dossier of the other five suspects will follow," it quoted East Timor Police chief Colonel Yusuf Muharam as saying on Tuesday.

An off-duty East Timorese soldier was beaten to death in the grounds of Dili's cathedral on December 24 as thousands of people gathered to welcome Roman Catholic bishop Carlos Belo back from Europe, where he had been a co-recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize.
